obligation: Bank recall of a misdirected wire (funds response)
citation: Fla. Stat. 670.211 (UCC Article 4A cancellation); FBI IC3 business email compromise guidance
trigger: A wire sent on fraudulent instructions (the buyer's closing wire, or an outgoing escrow payment)
deadline: Immediately on discovery. Once the receiving bank has accepted the payment order, cancellation needs that bank's agreement, so minutes matter
notify: Buyer's wire: the buyer calls their own bank and asks for a recall; the owner also alerts the escrow bank and the title company. Escrow payment: the owner calls the escrow bank's wire or fraud desk
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - operational; not a notification duty

obligation: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) complaint
trigger: Any business email compromise attempt or loss, whatever the amount
deadline: As soon as possible (voluntary; no legal deadline). The FBI states that prompt reporting may help banks and law enforcement freeze funds
notify: IC3 at www.ic3.gov with full banking details; the buyer files their own complaint too

trigger: Unauthorized access to electronic data containing personal information of Florida residents (for example a name with a driver license number in a stored image; or an email address with a password that permits access to the account)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email to an address in the records (never from the compromised mailbox)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the brokerage has no federal functional regulator, so the deemed-compliance path in 501.171(4)(g) is not available; counsel confirms

obligation: Florida notice not required after a no-harm determination
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the owner reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years and sent to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (copy of the determination)
applies_at_this_tier: Possible where the mailbox held no identity documents; counsel decides

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay individual notice for the period in the agency's written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination. 15 more days for the individual notice under (4) only, if good cause is given to the Department in writing within the 30 days
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of the notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - all records name about 260 Florida residents; recheck the count after any breach

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
applies_at_this_tier: No - all records together name about 350 individuals

obligation: Service provider breach notice to the owner (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent (the coordinator, the bookkeeper, or a SaaS vendor) has a breach of a system it maintains for the brokerage
deadline: Third-party agent must notify the owner no later than 10 days after determination; engagement terms may set a shorter time

trigger: Affected clients who live outside Florida (about 30% of buyers)
notify: Residents and, where required, state attorneys general or regulators
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residency of every affected person; counsel applies each state's law

obligation: Florida Real Estate Commission notice of an escrow dispute
citation: Fla. Stat. 475.25(1)(d)1.; Fla. Admin. Code r. 61J2-10.032(1)
trigger: A diverted or missing earnest money deposit leads to conflicting demands on funds in the sales escrow account, or the broker has good-faith doubt about who is entitled to them
deadline: Written notice to the Commission within 15 business days of the last demand or of the doubt; start a settlement procedure within 30 business days
notify: Florida Real Estate Commission (by the broker-owner)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the brokerage holds the deposit and demands conflict

obligation: Professional liability (errors and omissions) claim notice
trigger: A client loss or a claim that may be covered, including a funds transfer fraud claim
deadline: Per policy terms (usually as soon as practicable; call before hiring outside firms)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual; whether funds transfer fraud is covered is unconfirmed (owner action by 2026-10-31)

trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information involving 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the brokerage is not a financial institution (P03 section 1.1), and its records name about 350 individuals

trigger: Not a breach duty: adverse action based on a screening report
deadline: At the time of the decision
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for screening decisions (P10); listed here only so it is not confused with a breach notice

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed only: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-10-06; a one-person brokerage is unlikely to meet the proposed criteria

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
trigger: Considering an extortion or ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No for business email compromise; applies only if the incident turns into extortion

trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a public company
deadline: Within four business days after determining materiality
